page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The stamens
lines: Allium cepa, the onion, belongs to the family
Six stamens are arranged in two whorls of three
They are free from one another and epiphyllous,
that is, attached to the perianth.
steps.why: The anthers cannot be described without saying which stamens they belong to, and 3+3 epiphyllous is the Liliaceae pattern.
common_mistakes: Writing epipetalous. That word is for stamens on a corolla; Liliaceae has a perianth, so the word is epiphyllous.
Writing five stamens, which is the Solanaceae number.
steps.memory_tip: Onion is a Liliaceae plant: everything is in threes. Three plus three stamens, three carpels, three plus three tepals.
steps.margin_note: One line for the family, one for 3+3 and epiphyllous.

steps.label: The anthers
lines: Dithecous = two lobes, so four pollen sacs.
Basifixed = the filament is joined to the base of
Introrse = the anther opens towards the centre
steps.why: The four terms are the standard technical description of any anther, and each one is a separate tick.
common_mistakes: Writing versatile or dorsifixed. The onion anther is basifixed.
Writing extrorse. Introrse anthers face inward and favour self pollination.
steps.memory_tip: Four questions in order: how many lobes, where fixed, which way it faces, how it opens.
steps.margin_note: All four terms in one boxed line, then one line of meaning each.

insider_note: The question says anthers, but a bare four words looks thin. Give the 3+3 epiphyllous stamens first, then the four anther terms.
